submissions.name: paired-fresh-estimators
submissions.head: 6e9f018b0c619999a3822856ce655ca701d47411
submissions.title: Use independent estimator fits in paired statistical comparisons
submissions.body:
### Description

The four paired estimator-comparison helpers fit the same estimator objects repeatedly. Estimators that retain fitted state, including random forests with `warm_start=True`, can therefore reuse trees trained on an earlier split. A later test fold may already have influenced those trees, changing both the comparison statistic and its p-value.

This change clones each estimator before each independent fit in `paired_ttest_resampled`, `paired_ttest_kfold_cv`, `paired_ttest_5x2cv`, and `combined_ftest_5x2cv`. Scoring uses the fitted clones, and the supplied estimators retain their original state. The sampling, scoring, and statistical formulas stay the same. All four entry points share this cause and are covered together.

### Related issues or pull requests

Closes #1318.

Related work: #1242 adds a separate corrected resampled t-test; it does not change these existing four helpers. #1315 isolates bootstrap models in the separate `bias_variance_decomp` path. This PR addresses the independent repeated train/test fits above. Deduplication examined upstream PR refs, all fork heads, and their reachable intermediate changes to both source files; no equivalent change to these four entry points was found.

### Validation

- Exact upstream base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`.
- **23 of 28 new regression cases fail on unchanged source.** All 28 pass after the change.
- The tests compare real warm-start random forests with independently fitted models and separately computed test statistics. They cover regression and classification, pipelines, already-fitted inputs, cold-start controls, callable scoring, and unchanged caller state. A state-tracking estimator also verifies that the scorer never sees training observations retained from another fold.
- Existing and new tests for the four helpers: **41 passed**. Complete repository suite: **768 passed, 3 skipped**.
- Baseline and candidate ran in the same job using Python 3.11.18 and the unchanged frozen dependency lock.
- Complete repository isort/Black, changed-file Flake8, `git diff --check`, package build, and strict Twine metadata checks passed. The repository-wide Flake8 report retains existing findings and is not claimed as a clean lint gate.

[Baseline reproduction and complete validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43881707255/job/133348986775).

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added regression tests in the corresponding test directory.
- [x] Updated the affected public docstrings.
- [x] Ran focused and complete repository tests.
- [x] Checked formatting and style with the scope described above.

submissions.name: confusion-matrix-axes
submissions.head: 35a2bcd0bb6ee66be692e2e81369078259d32236
submissions.title: Keep confusion matrix labels and colorbars on the supplied axes
submissions.body:
### Description

`plot_confusion_matrix(axis=target)` draws the image on the supplied axes but uses pyplot's current axes for labels and ticks. If another subplot is current, its labels change instead. Supplying only `axis` also leaves the returned figure as `None`, and `colorbar=True` raises an `AttributeError`.

This change obtains the figure from the supplied axes and assigns ticks, axis labels, and colorbars directly to that axes. An explicitly supplied figure that does not own the axes is rejected before drawing. The default and figure-only forms remain supported.

The regression file is run as a separate command in both existing functional CI jobs. The repository's `norecursedirs` excludes plotting tests from ordinary recursive collection, so adding the path alongside the root argument did not actually collect it. The coverage job appends the explicit regression run to its existing coverage data.

### Related issues or pull requests

Closes #1319.

The complete reachable history for the affected module was checked across upstream PR refs and fork branches, including intermediate commits: 85 commits and 36 distinct source versions. Prior work introducing the figure/axes arguments does not correct this ownership problem; no equivalent fix was found.

### Validation

- Exact upstream base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`.
- **12 of 15 new regressions fail on the unchanged source**; all 15 pass with the patch.
- Cases cover multiple subplots and separate current figures, normalized and unnormalized matrices, explicit and inferred figure ownership, colorbars, tick/spine options, preserved unrelated axes, mismatched figure rejection, and existing construction forms.
- Complete repository suite: **740 passed, 3 skipped**; the **15 plotting regressions also pass in their separate invocation**.
- Baseline and candidate ran in the same job with Python 3.11.18 and the unchanged frozen lock.
- Complete repository isort/Black, changed-file Flake8, `git diff --check`, package build, and strict Twine checks passed. The repository-wide Flake8 report retains its existing findings and is not claimed as a clean gate.

[Reproduction and complete validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43883373059/job/133354886852).

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added regression tests in the corresponding test directory.
- [x] Documented figure and axes ownership.
- [x] Ran the full repository suite and the separate plotting regressions.
- [x] Checked formatting and style with the scope described above.
